quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Instead, slow down gradually or change lanes to prevent a collision.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your nerve impulses and body functions. This weakens your focus and alertness.

questions.question: What does a double yellow line with two solid lines two or more feet apart mean?

options.text: You may cross it to enter or exit a driveway.
You may not cross it for any reason.
You should treat it as a separate traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not cross it for any reason.
questions.explanation: Two solid double yellow lines spaced two or more feet apart act as a barrier. You cannot drive over this barrier or turn left across it, except at marked openings.

questions.question: Your wheels have gone off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel slightly left to edge back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the steering wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently. Slow down, check traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel hard—this can cause you to lose control or move into other lanes.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red traffic light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After coming to a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs prohibiting this turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Wet pavement is dangerous and can cause you to lose control. Slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Drive off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid slamming on the brakes or making sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using light braking.

questions.question: What is the benefit of keeping space around your vehicle?

options.text: Other drivers can cut in front of you, which improves traffic flow.
You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It inflates to protect you from injury in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your vehicle gives you time to safely respond if another driver makes a mistake. For example, extra space lets you brake or move out of the way if a vehicle veers into your lane.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even when you signal, do not assume that other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that weakens your judgment and makes your reflexes slow.

questions.question: You should always travel at:

options.text: The same speed as vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your driving speed should match road and weather conditions and must not exceed the speed limit. Slow down if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Increase your following distance to stop safely if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. Use your headlights properly according to the rules.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Rely on the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
Rely on the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Look multiple times if needed. Watch traffic in front of you and next to you.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the roadway or pavement edge, you should:

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
Turn back onto the roadway immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the roadway immediately. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually return to the roadway when it is safe.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle in a minor collision and cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Leave a note on the vehicle.
Report the collision to the city police or California Highway Patrol.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle you hit. Also report the collision to the local city police or California Highway Patrol.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop when you see this sign.

questions.question: When you approach a flashing red traffic light, you:

options.text: Are traveling in the wrong direction.
Must treat it like a stop sign.
May not proceed until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Which vehicles must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Tank trucks with hazardous materials labels.
Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat trailer.
Any vehicle with three or more axles weighing more than 4,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tank trucks with hazardous materials labels.
questions.explanation: Trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped orange signs warn of hazards. Orange signs are used in construction and maintenance areas.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers which laws they must follow. These signs are white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green words or symbols.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. Any trace of alcohol will result in a two-year license suspension and other penalties.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, drive at:

options.text: The same speed as freeway traffic.
The legal speed limit.
A slower speed than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Match the speed of freeway traffic when merging, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars pass you on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, stay in the right lanes unless passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic on an interstate, use the right lane.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending and you must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution.
Look to both sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to both sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross your path or traffic lines meet, look left and right to make sure no one is coming.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few mph faster than other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few mph slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic within posted speed limits. Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when some vehicles drive at different speeds.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: Can complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks must swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: A flashing yellow traffic signal means:

options.text: Treat it like a stop sign.
Stop and yield to all traffic before crossing.
Slow down and watch for hazards at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and watch for hazards at the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution. Slow down and be alert. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection, but you do not have to stop.

questions.question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks accelerate slowly and lose speed going uphill. Leave extra space behind trucks, especially on inclines.

questions.question: A police officer signals you to pull over, but you ignore the officer and flee. What is the penalty?

options.text: A fine up to $1,000.
Jail time in county jail for up to one year.
A warning and a citation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Jail time in county jail for up to one year.
questions.explanation: Fleeing from a police officer is a misdemeanor. You can be jailed in county jail for up to one year.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that turns in the direction of the arrow are not allowed.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when it first starts to rain. On a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
Test your tires' grip while going uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slowly and avoid fast turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Alcohol first affects:

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the areas of your brain that control judgment and skill. This is the first thing it impacts.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, drive:

options.text: Near the right-hand side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the centerline. Turn just before reaching the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue to find an alternate route to your destination.
Continue to the next exit and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Continue to the next exit. Other drivers do not expect vehicles to back up and this causes crashes.
